2607.05199.title: Reason, Reward, Refine: Step-Level Errors Corrections with Structured Feedback for Physics Reasoning in Small Language Models
2607.05199.paper_summary: Physics reasoning fails structurally in small language models: an error at any step propagates forward, corrupting every inference that follows. Limited domain knowledge, hallucination under multi-step derivation, and distributional sensitivity compound this failure. We propose a step-level reward framework that identifies the first reasoning error, generates targeted structured feedback, and trains the model to revise its solution via policy gradient with KL regularization, without exposing it to ground truth solutions as generation targets. Unlike annotation-dependent step-level methods, no preference data construction is required and the external verifier operates exclusively at training time. Across five physics benchmarks, our framework delivers accuracy gains of 17-20% over CoT prompting and 10-16% over the strongest baseline, reduces calculation errors from 56.9% to 23.5%, and reduces miscomprehension errors from 22.3% to 12.0% in the best observed cases. Conceptual errors reduce from 89.7% to 68.7%, yet persist as the hardest failure mode across all conditions.
2607.05199.paper_summary_zh: 物理推理在小型語言模型中結構性失效：任何步驟的錯誤都會向前傳播，腐蝕隨後的每一個推斷。有限的領域知識、多步推導下的幻覺以及分佈敏感性加劇了這一失敗。我們提出了一個步驟級獎勵框架，該框架識別第一個推理錯誤，生成針對性的結構化反饋，並通過政策梯度與KL正則化訓練模型修正其解決方案，而不將其暴露於作為生成目標的真實解決方案。與依賴註釋的步驟級方法不同，無需構建偏好數據，外部驗證者僅在訓練時運作。在五個物理基準測試中，我們的框架相較於CoT提示提供了17-20%的準確性提升，並在最強基線上提升了10-16%，將計算錯誤從56.9%降低至23.5%，並在最佳觀察案例中將誤解錯誤從22.3%降低至12.0%。概念錯誤從89.7%降低至68.7%，但在所有條件下仍然持續存在，成為最難的失敗模式。
